judgements.title: Expression: code vs natural language · baseline x3 / poles x1
summary: The code condition moves strongly toward code-like labels across all seven slots; the language condition moves strongly toward prose. The three baselines already vary in wording, grouping and detail, though each mixes expressions with explanatory sentences. Both extremes retain the main seven-slot subject coverage. Code preserves more exact identifiers and adds detail, but repeated @-style notation makes some groupings harder to read and can resemble a real API. Language reads more smoothly, but often drops signatures, field shapes and limits. The code canvas also has 30 cross-diagram edges, versus 19–23 in the baselines and 21 in language; that extra detail cannot be confidently attributed to the expression instruction.

Limitations

All 35 ASCII trees and the five supplied canvas records were assessed as generated artifacts. The code and language conditions have one output each, so within-condition variability and recurrence cannot be established; every selected difference is a tentative illustration with low attribution confidence. The three shared baselines show that alternative wording and detail can arise without a prompt change. Factual support means agreement among the supplied artifacts, not verification against source code. Some code-only specifics, including exact numeric limits, are not independently corroborated by the other outputs.

judgements.title: Focus: modular vs runtime state · baseline x3 / poles x1
summary: The single modular output (C4) moves toward contracts, type variants, public boundaries and dependencies. The single runtime output (C5) moves toward retained instances, related state, mutation and cleanup. The movement is clearest in MappingPage, FloatingBox, Controller edits and CanvasHistoryService. GridBox shifts modestly; DiagramService and Diagram remain largely organized around the same service and immutable value in all conditions. Across all seven slots, coverage of the main concepts remains comparable, and the pinned canvas layout and cross-diagram relationships remain similar. The three baselines already vary in wording, detail and organization, including examples of both requested emphases. C4 sometimes gives clearer boundaries but denser contract lists; C5 makes state lifetimes easier to follow but gives less space to some page capabilities. Neither extreme consistently eliminates repetition or fully separates meaningful groupings from broad headings.

Limitations

C4 and C5 each have one output, so within-condition variability and recurrence cannot be assessed. The six findings are tentative illustrations, with low attribution confidence; none shows that a baseline could never produce the same feature. Factual support was assessed only for consistency among the supplied trees, canvas manifest and pinned descriptions. No source code was supplied or verified. The fixed layout limits what placement differences can reveal.

judgements.title: Topology: shallow vs varied trees · baseline x3 / poles x1
summary: Both changes moved the trees in the requested direction. Across all seven slots, the three baselines reach two to four branch levels; shallow has one level in every slot, while varied reaches four to six. Baseline canvases contain 274–281 tree lines, shallow 234, and varied 279. Shallow retains many named components and relationships but compresses detail and makes long lists harder to scan. Varied preserves comparable coverage and offers clearer paths through some responsibilities, though a few deep chains may imply stronger parent-child relationships than the text establishes. Both extremes repeat concepts across related slots, as the baselines do.

Limitations

Each extreme has one output. Its within-condition variability and recurrence cannot be assessed, so the findings are tentative illustrations with low attribution confidence. The three baselines show ordinary variation in wording, detail and grouping; they do not establish that either observed shape could never occur under the baseline prompt. Factual support was assessed only for consistency within the supplied trees and canvas manifests. No source code was supplied for independent verification.

E04.description:
Baseline of the original four decision rules, using the seven ChangeSession v2 AgentContexts saved November 3, 2026. Three independent samples per case (21 total), gpt-6-sol/high. Output: the Proposed diagram changes ASCII tree only. Decision thresholds are unchanged; input access is adapted to pinned snapshots and the output contract is explicit. Deterministic syntax and strategy-count assessment is separate from generation; no architectural quality score or target strategy frequency.

Phase 2 adds seven derived contexts and 21 planned outputs using revised visible strategy rules. It separates patch versus redraw decisions from existing versus new canvas decisions, judges cumulative changes per diagram, and removes the rule to exhaust [1a]/[1b]/[2]/[3] before redraw along with historical N-detail diagram plans. Both prompt and input changed, so phase comparisons describe observed outcomes rather than an isolated prompt effect.
